entities.text: High Court Of Karnataka At Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This petition is filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail to the petitioners/accused Nos.1 and 2 in Cr.No.21/2023 of Shanivarasanthe police station, registered for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 506 r/w 34 IPC.

2. Heard both the sides and perused the material on record.
3.
The complaint averments would reveal that the complainant is the legally wedded wife of accused No.1.
Their marriage took place about 17 years ago and in their wedlock they have three female children.
The allegations are that accused No.1 is addicted to bad vices and subjecting the complainant to physical and mental harassment.

It is stated that since 10 months he has NC:
2023:KHC:19463 been residing separately in Bengaluru.
It is also alleged that without the knowledge of the complainant and her father-in-law, accused No.1 has taken away 100 gms. of gold belonging to the complainant.

It is further alleged that he is having illicit relationship with petitioner No.2 and when he was called to the police station on an earlier complaint, he admitted all his shortcomings and promised that he will not continue the same but later he sent the photographs etc., of his marriage with accused No.2 on her mobile number.

4. It is alleged that petitioner No.1 is having a relationship with petitioner No.2 and that he has married her and thereby giving mental harassment to the complainant and he has threatened the complainant and her children with dire consequences etc.
5. It appears that there is a serious matrimonial dispute between the complainant and petitioner No.1.
Their marriage is said to have taken place 17 years prior to lodging of the present complaint.
The allegations that NC: 2023:KHC:19463 petitioner No.1 has married petitioner No.2 etc., is a matter which has to be established in due course.

As per the complaint averments, he is staying separately in Bengaluru since last 10 months and the complainant is residing in Somawarapet,
Kodagu.
Custodial interrogation of the petitioners is not at all required.

In the facts and Mallikarjuna K M vs State Of Karnataka on 6 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72870252/
2 circumstances of the case, the petitioners can be directed to appear before the Investigating Officer and co-operate with the investigation.

sentences.text:
Hence, the following:
ORDER i. The petition is allowed.
ii. The petitioners/accused Nos.1 and 2 shall be released in the event of their arrest in Crime No.21/2023 registered at Shanivarasanthe Police Station, subject to following conditions:

( 1) Petitioners shall appear before the Investigation Officer within a period of one week from the date of receipt of a certified copy of the order and shall execute a personal bond in a sum of NC: 2023:KHC:19463 Rs.1,00,000/- each [Rupees one lakh only] with one surety for the likesum.
(2) Petitioners shall cooperate with the investigation and they shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses in any manner.

(3) Petitioners shall furnish proof of their residential address and shall inform the Investigating Officer/Court regarding change in the address, if any.
(4) Petitioners shall be regular in attending the Court proceedings.
Sd/-
